extracted.intended_audience: researchers in the health sciences preparing to submit preprints to medRxiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility criteria for submitting and posting complete but unpublished manuscripts (preprints) in medical, clinical, and related health sciences to the medRxiv server.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target content — preprints of complete but unpublished manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv is a free online archive and distribution server for complete but unpublished manuscripts (preprints) in the medical, clinical, and related health sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints are preliminary reports of work that have not been certified by peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research must describe human health research and follow scientific principles
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv is for the distribution of preprints ... that describe human health research conducted, analyzed, and interpreted according to scientific principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be soundly conducted and analyzed; medRxiv is not an endorsement of methods, assumptions, conclusions, or scientific quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Research articles, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, clinical research design protocols and data articles may be posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the primary content types medRxiv accepts for posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed content types
rubrics_metrics.description: MedRxiv is not intended for case reports (single or in series), narrative reviews, editorials, letters, opinion pieces and hypotheses that lack data, work not premised on modern biology/physiology or allopathic medicine, laboratory protocols/recipes, theses, term papers, textbook excerpts or individual components of research articles such as figures, tables, and datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not submit material that falls into these categories; such items are out of scope for posting on medRxiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic screening for offensive and non-scientific content
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles undergo a basic screening process for offensive and/or non-scientific content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions containing offensive language, pseudoscience, or clearly non-scientific material may be excluded during screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening for material that might pose a health risk or be dual use research of concern
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles are screened for material that might pose a health risk or be considered dual use research of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that could cause harm to public health or be misused for harmful purposes is subject to rejection; medRxiv assesses dual-use risks during screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism checks
rubrics_metrics.description: All articles are checked for plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts containing plagiarized material are subject to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not peer-reviewed — caution about clinical use and media reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints are preliminary reports of work that have not been certified by peer review. They should not be relied on to guide clinical practice or health-related behavior and should not be reported in news media as established information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users (clinicians, media, public) must interpret preprints cautiously; authors should not represent preprints as peer-reviewed evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No posting if already accepted/published/posted elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: A manuscript may be submitted prior to, or concurrently with, submission to a journal but will not be posted if it has already been accepted for publication, published, or posted elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should only submit manuscripts to medRxiv that have not already been formally accepted or published; concurrent journal submission is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision policy and versioning prior to journal acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit a revised version of a manuscript to medRxiv at any time (prior to the manuscript's acceptance for publication in a journal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised versions can be uploaded while the manuscript remains unpublished/uncertified by journal acceptance; version history will be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOI assignment and permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: Once posted on medRxiv, manuscripts receive a digital object identifier (DOI), so are discoverable, citable, and indexed by numerous search engines and third-party services and cannot be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting creates a permanent, citable record; authors should be aware that posted preprints cannot be removed from the server.

rubrics_metrics.name: medRxiv's discretion to decline posting
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv reserves the right to decline to post any preprint for any reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a submission meets formal criteria, medRxiv may still choose not to post it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope categorization — assignment to subject categories
rubrics_metrics.description: When posting an article, the author assigns it to one of the following categories: (followed by a long list: Addiction Medicine; Allergy and Immunology; ... Urology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must select the most appropriate category from medRxiv's health-sciences taxonomy when submitting; category affects discoverability and screening context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct transfer to journals (M2J) service
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv can save authors time in submitting papers to journals by transmitting their manuscript files and metadata directly from medRxiv to participating partner journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may use M2J to transfer submissions to listed partner journals instead of re-uploading files and re-entering metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy policy and collection/use of personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: bioRxiv and openRxiv are committed to protecting the privacy of authors, medRxiv Affiliates, and other users of the medRxiv submission system and website. Click to read the full Privacy Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and users should consult the privacy policy to understand how personal data are collected and used during submission and hosting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text & Data Mining (TDM) access
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv provides free and unrestricted access to all articles posted on the server. We believe this should apply not only to human readers but also to machine analysis of the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: medRxiv supports machine analysis of content and provides resources to facilitate programmatic access and TDM of posted articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-affiliate role in screening and advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: medRxiv Affiliates are members of the life sciences community who provide feedback on the service, act as advocates, and help in screening material submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening and community moderation may involve volunteers/affiliates; authors may interact with or be affected by affiliate feedback.
